author: opencode-worker-3
text: CONFIRMED root cause (deterministic, not candidate 2/3): (1) lichen_link_epoch_advance_for_boot latches s_advanced — every soft reinit in one boot returns the SAME boot epoch E1 (epoch_persist.c:126-131). (2) lichen_link_load_key sets ctx->tx_seq = 0 (link_ctx.c, 'ctx->tx_seq = 0' after has_key assignment) and lichen_l2_load_key then overrides the random load epoch with the latched boot epoch (lichen_l2_key.c:137-139 lichen_link_set_epoch(boot_epoch)). (3) full_ping commits (E1, seq0=Echo Request, seq1=Reply) under the test pubkey; queue_stats' reprovision reloads the SAME seed -> same pubkey, tx_seq reset 0, same E1 -> udp's first frame is (E1, seq0) = exact replay. Production analog: ANY same-key re-provision after a keyed-context wipe (disable, watchdog reinit) reuses (epoch,seq) against receivers that still hold that pubkey's replay window. RECOMMENDED FIX (link-layer, needs owner sign-off on nonce semantics): persist the tuple at TEARDOWN (save_tuple currently runs only inside load_key, post-reset, so the seq history is already lost when the ctx is wiped) and in lichen_link_load_key restore ctx->tx_seq from the persisted tuple when tuple.ed25519_pk == newly derived pk (fresh keypair keeps seq 0 — new replay identity). Alternative: force an epoch advance whenever a KEYED context is torn down — correct but burns the 8-bit epoch space per disable/enable cycle (255 cycles to exhaustion), so the tuple-restore path is preferred. The replay_table_init on enable does NOT mask this: the RX table is fresh, but any RECEIVER that saw the earlier frames (real deployment) rejects.
